counterexample: n = 3: L(4) = 3, L(3) = 2, lambda(3) = 0 (Zeckendorf(3) + F_1 is already Zeckendorf); fails for 288 of the first 300 n (EXP-C19-02). Longest games avoid early normalisation, so they do not pass through Zeckendorf(n).
statement: L(n + 1) = L(n) + lambda(n), where lambda(n) is the longest game from the Zeckendorf representation of n plus one extra F_1.
title: H-C19-4: the longest game is built by inserting one chip at a time (refuted)
